primitives.name: PromptTemplate
primitives.purpose: Declare a named, versioned, parameterized prompt whose text, variables, and target model are pinned so two runs of the same version produce identical rendered payloads.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Mapping

class PromptTemplate(Protocol):
    name: str
    version: int
    target_model: str
    variables: tuple[str, ...]
    def render(self, values: Mapping[str, str]) -> str: ...
    def fingerprint(self) -> str: ...
invariants: Rendered output MUST be byte-identical across two calls with the same (version, values) pair.
A published version MUST NEVER be mutated; changes SHALL produce a new integer version.
render() MUST raise when a declared variable is missing from values and MUST NEVER silently inject an empty string.
fingerprint() MUST cover template text, target_model, and variable names so drift in any of them SHALL change the fingerprint.
Variable interpolation MUST use explicit delimiters and CANNOT treat unescaped user input as template syntax.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream code registers a new prompt by declaring a subclass or a decorator-annotated factory; the registry rejects a register() call that reuses (name, version) so that every published pair resolves to exactly one template object.
primitives.consumption_example:
from typing import Protocol

def run_extraction(tpl: PromptTemplate, payload: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    rendered = tpl.render(payload)
    fp = tpl.fingerprint()
    return f"model={tpl.target_model} fp={fp} text={rendered}"

sources.locator: Prompt Management section: versioned prompts, labels, compile()
weave.Prompt / StringPrompt reference — versioned prompt objects

primitives.why_essential: Without a pinned, diffable prompt object, evaluations cannot be reproduced and production incidents cannot be traced back to the exact text that generated the bad output.
alternatives_considered: Inline f-strings per call site — loses version identity and makes rollback impossible.
Loading prompts from plain files on disk — no fingerprint, no immutability guarantee, no named versions.

primitives.name: ModelRegistry
primitives.purpose: Resolve a logical model handle to a concrete provider endpoint plus declared capabilities (context window, tool-use, streaming, max output tokens) so call sites never hardcode provider identifiers.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class ModelSpec(Protocol):
    handle: str
    provider: str
    context_window_tokens: int
    max_output_tokens: int
    supports_tools: bool
    supports_streaming: bool
    modality: Literal["text", "vision", "audio"]

class ModelRegistry(Protocol):
    def resolve(self, handle: str) -> ModelSpec: ...
    def list_handles(self) -> tuple[str, ...]: ...
invariants: resolve() MUST raise when the handle is unknown and MUST NEVER fall back to a default model.
A ModelSpec returned by resolve() MUST be immutable for the lifetime of a process.
context_window_tokens and max_output_tokens MUST reflect the provider's published limit, NEVER a soft internal estimate.
Two distinct handles CANNOT map to the same provider endpoint unless their capability tuples also differ.
The registry SHALL be the only component that reads provider identifiers from configuration; call sites MUST use handles.
primitives.extension_contract: A downstream skill registers a new model by providing a ModelSpec adapter for the provider and calling register(handle, spec); adapters MUST be pure metadata plus a client factory and CANNOT embed business logic.

sources.locator: model_cost_map.json + router.Router configuration (provider, max_tokens)
Model Registry: linked artifacts with alias + metadata

primitives.why_essential: Call sites that embed provider names and token limits cannot be retargeted, split-tested, or priced without touching every feature; the registry centralizes those facts.
alternatives_considered: Environment variables per feature — fan-out explodes and drifts between services.
Hardcoded provider SDK imports at call site — cannot switch providers without code changes.

primitives.name: VectorStore
primitives.purpose: Expose upsert, similarity search, metadata filter, and delete over embedded documents with per-tenant scoping so retrieval augmentation cannot leak rows across tenants or return deleted content.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Sequence

class VectorHit(Protocol):
    doc_id: str
    score: float
    metadata: Mapping[str, str]

class VectorStore(Protocol):
    def upsert(self, tenant_id: str, doc_id: str, embedding: Sequence[float], metadata: Mapping[str, str]) -> None: ...
    def search(self, tenant_id: str, query_embedding: Sequence[float], top_k: int, filter: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[VectorHit, ...]: ...
    def delete(self, tenant_id: str, doc_id: str) -> bool: ...
invariants: search() MUST scope results to the supplied tenant_id and MUST NEVER return a hit owned by a different tenant.
upsert() SHALL be idempotent on (tenant_id, doc_id); a second call with identical embedding CANNOT create a duplicate row.
delete() MUST remove the document from subsequent search results within a bounded staleness window declared by the adapter.
Embedding dimensionality MUST be validated against the store's configured dimension and MUST raise on mismatch.
Metadata filter keys MUST be constrained to a registered schema; arbitrary free-form keys are FORBIDDEN to prevent index explosion.
primitives.extension_contract: New backends (pgvector, Qdrant, etc.) plug in as adapters implementing the VectorStore protocol; adapters register with the DI container and MUST implement the tenant-scoping invariant even when the underlying engine has no native tenancy.

sources.locator: LLM08: Excessive Agency / LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure — tenant isolation on retrieved context
Resources & Tools: structured access to external data with scoped permissions

primitives.why_essential: Retrieval augmentation is the single largest cross-tenant leak vector in LLM apps; centralizing the store ensures tenancy, dimension checks, and delete propagation are enforced once.
alternatives_considered: Direct SQL calls to pgvector per feature — tenant filter is easy to forget in one of N queries.
Embedding a provider SDK at call site — cannot swap backends or add deletion propagation uniformly.

primitives.name: InputGuardrail
primitives.purpose: Intercept user input before it reaches a model and reject, redact, or transform it according to deterministic rules (PII, injection markers) and optional LLM-judged classifications.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class GuardDecision(Protocol):
    action: Literal["allow", "redact", "block"]
    reason: str
    redacted_text: str | None

class InputGuardrail(Protocol):
    name: str
    def evaluate(self, text: str, context: dict[str, str]) -> GuardDecision: ...
invariants: evaluate() MUST be deterministic for a given (text, context) unless the guardrail declares itself probabilistic via its name suffix.
A BLOCK decision MUST halt the pipeline; the caller CANNOT silently downgrade it to allow.
REDACT decisions SHALL return redacted_text and MUST NEVER return the original text under a redact verdict.
Every decision MUST carry a non-empty reason so downstream audit can explain the verdict.
Guardrails MUST NEVER store raw blocked inputs in logs in clear form; storage SHALL be hashed or truncated.
primitives.extension_contract: Projects add a guardrail by implementing the InputGuardrail protocol and registering it in an ordered chain; the chain runs rules as a pipeline of interceptors, stopping at the first BLOCK verdict.

sources.locator: LLM01: Prompt Injection — input classifiers and escaping
LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure — PII redaction before prompt assembly

primitives.why_essential: Prompt injection and PII leakage must be screened before any model call; leaving this per-feature guarantees inconsistent coverage and silent bypasses.
alternatives_considered: Regex inside each endpoint — impossible to centrally audit or update when threat patterns change.
Relying on the model itself to refuse — bypassable and not auditable.

primitives.name: OutputGuardrail
primitives.purpose: Inspect model output after generation and reject, rewrite, or annotate it against schema, policy, and safety rules before the caller or downstream tools receive it.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class OutputVerdict(Protocol):
    action: Literal["pass", "rewrite", "block"]
    reason: str
    replacement: str | None

class OutputGuardrail(Protocol):
    name: str
    def evaluate(self, output: str, schema_ref: str | None) -> OutputVerdict: ...
invariants: evaluate() MUST reject output that fails schema validation when schema_ref is provided; CANNOT pass malformed JSON as pass.
A BLOCK verdict MUST prevent the output from being returned to the caller or passed to any downstream tool.
REWRITE verdicts MUST provide a replacement; a replacement of None under rewrite SHALL be treated as a contract violation.
Output guardrails MUST NEVER execute tool calls embedded in the output before passing safety checks.
Every verdict SHALL be recorded with the guardrail name so post-hoc analysis can attribute the decision.
primitives.extension_contract: Additional output checks register as adapters in an ordered chain; downstream libraries compose schema, policy, and safety checks by appending adapters that implement the OutputGuardrail protocol.

sources.locator: LLM02: Insecure Output Handling — validate before downstream use
LLM09: Overreliance — programmatic verification of model output

primitives.why_essential: Treating model text as trusted is the second-leading class of LLM vulnerability; a shared output guard ensures every call path applies the same checks before tool execution or user display.
alternatives_considered: Ad-hoc JSON parsing at each call site — silent failures and no shared policy.
Relying on function-calling schemas alone — does not catch policy or safety issues, only shape.

primitives.name: HumanCheckpoint
primitives.purpose: Block an agent workflow at a named step until an authorized human approves, rejects, or edits the proposed action, persisting the decision and the reviewer identity.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class CheckpointDecision(Protocol):
    verdict: Literal["approved", "rejected", "edited"]
    reviewer_id: str
    edited_payload: dict[str, str] | None
    decided_at_iso: str

class HumanCheckpoint(Protocol):
    step_name: str
    def request(self, payload: dict[str, str], required_role: str) -> str: ...
    def await_decision(self, ticket_id: str, timeout_seconds: int) -> CheckpointDecision: ...
invariants: await_decision() MUST block until a reviewer with the required_role acts or the timeout is reached; an anonymous approval SHALL be rejected.
A checkpoint ticket CANNOT be approved by the same identity that created the ticket when required_role declares segregation.
Every decision MUST be persisted with reviewer_id and decided_at_iso before the call returns.
edited payloads SHALL be returned verbatim to the workflow and MUST NEVER be merged silently with the original payload.
On timeout, request SHALL default to reject rather than continue; silent continuation is FORBIDDEN.
primitives.extension_contract: Teams plug in notification transports (email, Slack, in-app) as adapters implementing a notify() hook; the checkpoint core handles ticket persistence and decision recording while adapters only deliver the notification.

sources.locator: LLM08: Excessive Agency — require human-in-the-loop for high-impact actions
Sampling / elicitation flow: client-mediated approval of model-proposed actions

primitives.why_essential: High-impact actions proposed by an LLM must not execute without authorized human approval; a shared primitive makes the approval path auditable and consistent.
alternatives_considered: Inline confirmation prompts in each feature — skip-once attitude erodes the safety net.
External ticket queue with manual linking — loses binding between decision and the proposed payload.

primitives.name: EvalHarness
primitives.purpose: Execute a golden dataset against a prompt-plus-model pair and compute graded verdicts via deterministic metrics and optional judge models, emitting a replayable run record.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Sequence

class EvalCase(Protocol):
    case_id: str
    inputs: dict[str, str]
    expected: dict[str, str]

class EvalResult(Protocol):
    case_id: str
    scores: dict[str, float]
    passed: bool

class EvalHarness(Protocol):
    def run(self, dataset: Sequence[EvalCase], prompt_version: int, model_handle: str) -> tuple[EvalResult, ...]: ...
    def aggregate(self, results: Sequence[EvalResult]) -> dict[str, float]: ...
invariants: run() MUST execute every case in the dataset and MUST NEVER short-circuit on the first failure.
Each EvalResult SHALL reference the exact prompt_version and model_handle used; rerunning with the same pair MUST yield equivalent scores modulo sampling noise declared in metadata.
Judge-model scores MUST be recorded alongside the judge's prompt_version so eval drift is attributable.
An eval run CANNOT be marked passing while any case fails a metric declared blocking.
Dataset modifications SHALL produce a new dataset version; the harness MUST reject runs referencing a mutated dataset id.
primitives.extension_contract: Custom metrics register as callables returning a float score and a pass flag; teams add new metrics via a decorator that the harness discovers at load, and judge models plug in as adapters exposing an evaluate() method.
primitives.consumption_example:
def ci_gate(h: EvalHarness, cases: list[EvalCase]) -> bool:
    results = h.run(cases, prompt_version=7, model_handle="planner-v2")
    agg = h.aggregate(results)
    return agg.get("exact_match", 0.0) >= 0.8

primitives.why_essential: Without a shared eval primitive, every team builds an incompatible grading loop and regressions ship unnoticed; a common harness lets every skill gate releases on the same evidence.
alternatives_considered: Hand-rolled pytest comparisons — no run linkage to prompt/model identity, no aggregation.
Spreadsheet review of sample outputs — neither deterministic nor repeatable.

primitives.name: TokenMeter
primitives.purpose: Record prompt tokens, completion tokens, cache-read tokens, and provider-reported cost for every model call, attributing each unit of consumption to a tenant, user, and feature label.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol

class TokenUsage(Protocol):
    prompt_tokens: int
    completion_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    cache_write_tokens: int
    cost_usd: float

class TokenMeter(Protocol):
    def record(self, model_handle: str, usage: TokenUsage, labels: dict[str, str]) -> None: ...
    def sum(self, labels: dict[str, str], window_seconds: int) -> TokenUsage: ...
invariants: record() MUST be called exactly once per completed model call; double-counting is FORBIDDEN.
cost_usd SHALL be computed from provider-reported counts via the ModelRegistry's pricing, NEVER estimated from string length.
labels MUST include a tenant identifier; an unlabelled record CANNOT be accepted.
cache_read_tokens MUST be reported separately from prompt_tokens so cache hit ratios are auditable.
sum() queries SHALL respect tenant isolation and MUST NEVER aggregate across tenant boundaries without explicit cross-tenant scope.
primitives.extension_contract: Backends (Prometheus, a ledger table, a provider gateway webhook) implement a sink adapter that register with the meter; the meter fans out record() events to every registered sink without requiring call-site changes.
primitives.consumption_example:
def after_call(meter: TokenMeter, usage: TokenUsage, tenant: str, feature: str) -> None:
    meter.record("planner-v2", usage, {"tenant": tenant, "feature": feature})

primitives.why_essential: Model cost is the highest variable expense in LLM products and the only defense against runaway multi-tenant abuse; per-feature attribution must be captured at one chokepoint.
alternatives_considered: Reading invoices monthly — too slow to catch abuse or runaway loops.
Per-feature log lines parsed later — lossy and not tenant-attributable in real time.

primitives.name: ResponseCache
primitives.purpose: Reuse a prior model response when a call resolves to the same cache key (exact prompt hash or semantic embedding match within a threshold), returning the cached payload.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class CacheKey(Protocol):
    mode: Literal["exact", "semantic"]
    value: str
    namespace: str

class ResponseCache(Protocol):
    def lookup(self, key: CacheKey, threshold: float | None = None) -> str | None: ...
    def store(self, key: CacheKey, response: str, ttl_seconds: int) -> None: ...
invariants: lookup() under mode=exact MUST hit only when the key value matches byte-for-byte; near-matches CANNOT be returned.
lookup() under mode=semantic MUST require a threshold argument and SHALL miss when similarity falls below it.
Cached payloads MUST NEVER be served across namespace boundaries; a tenant namespace is FORBIDDEN to share entries with another.
store() SHALL respect TTL; expired entries MUST be filtered out at lookup time, not only at write time.
Cache hits MUST be reported to TokenMeter with cache_read_tokens so cost accounting remains truthful.
primitives.extension_contract: Backends (Redis, SQLite, Postgres) plug in as adapters implementing lookup/store; a decorator on call sites binds a ResponseCache instance to a function so memoization is declarative rather than manual.

sources.locator: Cache feature: keyed by request hash with bucketed TTL, reporting cache hits in usage
Observation metadata: cache_hit flag propagated on generation events

primitives.why_essential: Repeated or near-repeated prompts dominate real-world LLM traffic; a shared cache primitive saves cost and latency while preserving tenancy and audit properties.
alternatives_considered: No cache — pays full price for duplicate traffic in chat and batch workloads.
Per-feature Redis keys — re-implements tenancy, TTL, and hit accounting each time.

primitives.name: ModelRouter
primitives.purpose: Select a concrete model handle for a request based on declared policy (cheapest-first, quality-floor, tenant override) and fall back to the next candidate on rate limit, timeout, or provider error.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Sequence

class RoutePolicy(Protocol):
    candidates: tuple[str, ...]
    quality_floor: str
    budget_usd_cents: int

class ModelRouter(Protocol):
    def choose(self, policy: RoutePolicy, tenant_id: str) -> str: ...
    def failover(self, exhausted: Sequence[str], policy: RoutePolicy) -> str: ...
invariants: choose() MUST honour the policy's quality_floor; a candidate below the floor CANNOT be returned even when it is cheapest.
failover() MUST NEVER return a handle present in the exhausted list within the same request scope.
The router SHALL refuse to route when the tenant's BudgetGuard reports the tenant is over budget.
Routing decisions MUST be recorded with the chosen handle and reason so fallback chains are reconstructable.
Tenant overrides SHALL take precedence over global policy and CANNOT be silently ignored by default policy.
primitives.extension_contract: Projects add custom strategies (e.g., canary routing) by implementing a RoutePolicy provider and registering it; the router composes registered strategies via a middleware chain whose order is declared at boot.

sources.locator: Router class: model_list with weights, fallbacks, and rpm/tpm limits
Config: routing strategies (loadbalance, fallback, conditional) and retry semantics

primitives.why_essential: Provider outages and rate limits are routine; single-provider call sites either crash or silently degrade, while a shared router expresses failover policy declaratively.
alternatives_considered: Try/except around one provider SDK — no visibility into why it fell back, no policy.
Client-side round-robin — cannot honour quality floors or tenant overrides.

primitives.name: ToolSchema
primitives.purpose: Describe a callable tool by name, JSON-schema input, side-effect class, and required scopes so function calling validates arguments and enforces authorization before executing the tool.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class ToolSchema(Protocol):
    name: str
    description: str
    input_schema: dict[str, object]
    side_effect: Literal["read", "write", "external"]
    required_scopes: tuple[str, ...]
    def validate_arguments(self, args: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]: ...
invariants: validate_arguments() MUST reject arguments that fail the input_schema and MUST NEVER coerce missing required fields to defaults.
A tool with side_effect=write or external CANNOT be invoked without the caller presenting every entry in required_scopes.
The schema name MUST match the executable binding one-to-one; two tools sharing a name are FORBIDDEN.
Tool descriptions SHALL be static strings; dynamic descriptions that change per call are FORBIDDEN to keep model behaviour reproducible.
validate_arguments() MUST NEVER perform side effects; it is a pure validator and the caller SHALL trigger execution explicitly.
primitives.extension_contract: Each new tool is registered by implementing the ToolSchema protocol and binding it to a handler via a decorator; the registry publishes the JSON-schema list to the model prompt and rejects duplicate names at load time.

sources.locator: Tools: name, description, inputSchema (JSON Schema) and capability negotiation

primitives.why_essential: Function calling without argument validation and scope checks is the primary agent-excess-agency risk; a shared schema primitive enforces both uniformly across every tool.
alternatives_considered: Passing raw model output to Python functions — argument types and authorization silently elided.
Per-tool ad-hoc validation code — drifts and skips edge cases in one tool out of N.

primitives.name: LlmTrace
primitives.purpose: Emit structured spans for each model call with attributes aligned to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions so token counts, model identity, and prompt/response linkage land in traces consistently.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, ContextManager

class LlmTrace(Protocol):
    def start(self, operation: str, model_handle: str, prompt_fingerprint: str) -> ContextManager["LlmSpan"]: ...

class LlmSpan(Protocol):
    def set_usage(self, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> None: ...
    def set_finish_reason(self, reason: str) -> None: ...
    def record_error(self, code: str, message: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Every model call SHALL open exactly one LlmTrace span; unspanned calls are FORBIDDEN.
Span attribute names MUST match the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens).
Spans MUST record prompt_fingerprint so the trace can be correlated with the PromptTemplate version that generated it.
On provider error the span MUST call record_error before exiting; swallowing the error without recording is FORBIDDEN.
Child tool-call spans MUST nest under the model-call span so the causal chain is reconstructable end-to-end.
primitives.extension_contract: The trace core is a thin adapter over an OpenTelemetry tracer; projects add exporters (OTLP, Langfuse, vendor-specific) by registering them against the OTel provider without modifying call-site code.
primitives.consumption_example:
def call_model(tracer: LlmTrace, fp: str):
    with tracer.start("completion", "planner-v2", fp) as span:
        span.set_usage(1200, 340)
        span.set_finish_reason("stop")

primitives.why_essential: Without standardized spans, cost, latency, and quality questions cannot be answered with one query; aligning on OTel GenAI conventions makes every vendor-neutral dashboard work out of the box.

primitives.name: BudgetGuard
primitives.purpose: Enforce per-tenant, per-feature, and per-time-window spending ceilings by consulting the TokenMeter and rejecting or throttling new model calls when the configured budget is exhausted.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class BudgetVerdict(Protocol):
    action: Literal["allow", "throttle", "deny"]
    remaining_usd_cents: int
    window_seconds: int

class BudgetGuard(Protocol):
    def check(self, tenant_id: str, feature: str, est_cost_usd_cents: int) -> BudgetVerdict: ...
    def set_limit(self, tenant_id: str, feature: str, ceiling_usd_cents: int, window_seconds: int) -> None: ...
invariants: check() MUST deny when est_cost_usd_cents + already-spent exceeds ceiling_usd_cents within the window.
remaining_usd_cents MUST NEVER be reported as negative; exhaustion is represented by action=deny with remaining=0.
set_limit() SHALL require both a ceiling and a window; an open-ended limit is FORBIDDEN.
Throttle action MUST be deterministic with respect to the configured strategy so two services applying the same policy agree on throttle timing.
A missing tenant or feature binding MUST default to deny rather than allow; unknown-scope billing is FORBIDDEN.
primitives.extension_contract: Teams plug in limit stores (Redis counter, database row) as adapters implementing increment/read; new throttle strategies (leaky bucket, token bucket) register as middleware that the guard invokes between check and its verdict.

sources.locator: Rate limits and cost ceilings per user / organization with window resets
Virtual keys: per-key budget ceilings and enforcement at gateway

primitives.why_essential: Without a budget guard, a single runaway loop or abusive tenant can consume a month of budget in hours; ceiling enforcement has to live adjacent to the token meter to be believed.
alternatives_considered: Post-hoc alerts from billing dashboards — triggers after the money is already spent.
Fixed per-call rate limit only — rate limits do not represent spend, only frequency.

primitives.name: PromptInjectionFilter
primitives.purpose: Quarantine untrusted text (retrieved documents, tool outputs, user messages) by wrapping it in delimiters and stripping instruction-like fragments that target the model.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

class QuarantinedText(Protocol):
    kind: Literal["user", "retrieved", "tool_output"]
    wrapped: str
    stripped_fragments: tuple[str, ...]

class PromptInjectionFilter(Protocol):
    def quarantine(self, raw: str, kind: str) -> QuarantinedText: ...
invariants: quarantine() MUST wrap the raw text in delimiters the model is instructed to treat as data; raw insertion into system prompts is FORBIDDEN.
Fragments matching known instruction patterns (imperative directives, role-override phrases) SHALL be stripped and the removed text returned in stripped_fragments for audit.
The filter MUST NEVER execute or interpret the raw text; it only transforms text.
Every quarantined block SHALL declare its kind so downstream guardrails can apply kind-specific rules (retrieved vs user vs tool_output).
Quarantining is NEVER optional for retrieved or tool_output content; skipping the filter on those sources is FORBIDDEN.
primitives.extension_contract: Projects extend the pattern catalog by registering stripping rules as adapters; each rule implements a pattern matcher and a redactor, composed into a pipeline the filter runs in declared order.
primitives.consumption_example:
def build_context(f: PromptInjectionFilter, snippets: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[str]:
    return [f.quarantine(text, kind).wrapped for kind, text in snippets]

sources.locator: LLM01: Prompt Injection — indirect injection via retrieved content and tool outputs
Server-provided resources: treated as untrusted context, surfaced with provenance

primitives.why_essential: Indirect prompt injection through retrieved documents and tool outputs is the leading unpatched LLM failure mode; a shared quarantine primitive ensures every context-assembly path applies the same defense.
alternatives_considered: String concatenation of retrieved content into system prompt — directly exploitable.
Relying on model refusal — inconsistent and not auditable.

cross_cutting_insights: Token accounting and budget enforcement must share identity: TokenMeter records what BudgetGuard decides against, and both pivot on the tenant/feature label pair used by ModelRouter.

Prompt identity is the linchpin — PromptTemplate.fingerprint threads through EvalHarness run records, LlmTrace span attributes, and ResponseCache keys so every observation is pinned to an exact text version.

Defense against LLM01 injection requires two coordinated primitives: PromptInjectionFilter wraps untrusted context, while InputGuardrail rejects or redacts before prompt assembly; neither is sufficient alone.

Model substitution safety depends on ModelRegistry (capability truth) plus ModelRouter (policy) plus BudgetGuard (economic guardrail); call sites that bypass any of the three silently break reproducibility or cost controls.

Output trust is the OWASP LLM02/LLM08 dividing line: OutputGuardrail validates shape and safety before ToolSchema.validate_arguments gates side effects, and HumanCheckpoint inserts when the action is high-impact.

Observability convergence around OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes lets vendor backends (Langfuse, W&B Weave, Portkey, Helicone) ingest the same span data without per-vendor instrumentation code at call sites.

Multi-tenancy is a non-local property of the LLM venous system: VectorStore, ResponseCache, TokenMeter, and BudgetGuard each enforce tenant isolation, and any single bypass constitutes a cross-tenant data or cost leak.
gaps_observed: SKILL-001 lacks a first-class PromptTemplate object with versioned fingerprint; prompts today are inline strings without diffable identity.
No shared VectorStore primitive exists in SKILL-001, so tenant scoping and deletion propagation are re-solved per feature.
No OutputGuardrail chain is wired to the tool-call dispatcher; OWASP LLM02 validation is implicit and per-endpoint.
HumanCheckpoint is absent; high-impact actions that should require approval currently execute on model output alone.
TokenMeter and BudgetGuard are not factored out, so cost attribution relies on post-hoc log parsing rather than a call-time ledger.
LlmTrace does not yet align with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention attribute names, blocking vendor-neutral observability backends.
PromptInjectionFilter is missing, meaning retrieved documents and tool outputs are concatenated into prompts without a quarantine step.
